options.a: Known latent defects or conditions that could significantly affect value or desirability
options.b: The seller's reasons for selling and the lowest price the seller is willing to accept
options.c: The racial or religious makeup of the neighborhood surrounding the property
options.d: That a former occupant of the home was living with HIV or AIDS

distractorExplanations.b: Seller motivation and bottom-line price are confidential client information, not material property facts.
distractorExplanations.c: Discussing neighborhood racial or religious composition is steering under the Fair Housing Act, not a required disclosure.
distractorExplanations.d: HIV/AIDS is a protected disability under federal fair housing law; it is not a material property fact to disclose.

az-real-estate-readiness-check-agency-la.explanation: Material property defects and legally required disclosures must be shared; confidential motivations may be protected. Disclosure duties follow applicable law.

options.a: Deadlines are targets, and a party may perform within a reasonable time after
options.b: The closing date is binding, but contingency deadlines may be extended freely
options.c: The contract must close within 30 days of acceptance to remain enforceable
options.d: Contract dates and times are critical and late performance may be a breach

distractorExplanations.a: That is the reasonable-time standard that applies when the clause is absent; the clause makes dates strict.
distractorExplanations.b: The clause applies to all contract dates, including contingency deadlines, not just the closing date.
distractorExplanations.c: The clause enforces the dates the parties chose; it does not impose a fixed 30-day closing period.

options.a: Recording the deed in the public land records
options.b: Having the grantor's signature notarized
options.c: Delivering the signed deed to the grantee
options.d: Purchasing an owner's title insurance policy

distractorExplanations.b: Acknowledgment makes a deed eligible for recording but by itself gives no notice to the public.
distractorExplanations.c: Delivery and acceptance transfer title between the parties; recording is what gives notice to the world.
distractorExplanations.d: Title insurance protects the insured against covered defects; it does not give public notice of the deed.

options.a: Lets the lender demand full payoff if the property is sold
options.b: Requires extra payment if the borrower pays off early
options.c: Lets the lender accelerate the full balance after a borrower default
options.d: Charges a fee when the borrower's monthly payment arrives late

distractorExplanations.a: That is a due-on-sale (alienation) clause, which is triggered by a transfer rather than an early payoff.
distractorExplanations.c: That is an acceleration clause, which is triggered by default rather than by voluntary early payoff.
distractorExplanations.d: That is a late-payment charge; a prepayment penalty applies when the borrower pays early, not late.

az-real-estate-readiness-check-finance-a.explanation: Prepayment penalties charge for early payoff when permitted by the loan terms and law. The penalty applies only when the note and law allow it.

options.a: Obtain the highest possible price even when the seller directs a quicker sale
options.b: Promote the seller's interests with loyalty, care, and obedience within the law
options.c: Treat buyer and seller with equal advocacy so both receive fair representation
options.d: Advise the seller on title and tax matters as the seller's legal representative

distractorExplanations.a: Price is not the top duty; obedience requires following the seller's lawful instruction to favor a quick sale.
distractorExplanations.c: Equal advocacy describes a neutral or dual role; a listing broker owes loyalty to the seller client, not both sides.
distractorExplanations.d: Confuses agency with legal practice; a broker must refer title and tax questions to an attorney or CPA.

options.a: At closing, when the settlement agent reviews the final agency paperwork
options.b: Once the purchase contract is accepted and both parties have signed it
options.c: Only if one of the parties is an existing client rather than a customer
options.d: Before or as soon as practicable when the dual/designated relationship arises

distractorExplanations.a: Closing is far too late; informed consent must come before the licensee acts for both parties.
distractorExplanations.b: Waiting until acceptance means both parties negotiated without knowing the licensee's divided loyalty.
distractorExplanations.c: Disclosure is triggered by the dual or designated relationship itself, not by whether a party was a prior client.

az-real-estate-readiness-check-agency-la.explanation: Agency disclosure timing is early—when the dual or designated relationship is created or contemplated. Exact timing follows the applicable license-law rules.

options.a: Suggest an offer amount, since helping the buyer also helps close the sale
options.b: Avoid acting as the buyer's advocate and stay within the listing agency role
options.c: Share the seller's lowest acceptable price so the buyer can offer efficiently
options.d: Give a price opinion as long as the buyer has signed the agency disclosure form

distractorExplanations.a: Recommending an offer amount is buyer advocacy that conflicts with the listing agent's loyalty to the seller.
distractorExplanations.c: Revealing the seller's bottom line breaches the confidentiality duty owed to the seller client.
distractorExplanations.d: Signing an agency disclosure does not create buyer representation; the agent still represents only the seller.

az-real-estate-readiness-check-agency-la.explanation: Listing agents represent the seller; advocacy for a buyer requires a proper agency shift/disclosure. If allowed, the brokerage may properly create buyer agency with required disclosures.

options.a: Lacked consideration or a legal purpose
options.b: Made only an oral agreement to buy land
options.c: Later found a better deal on another home
options.d: Was induced by fraud or was a minor

distractorExplanations.a: A contract missing consideration or a legal purpose is void or unenforceable, not voidable at one party's option.
distractorExplanations.b: An oral land contract is unenforceable under the statute of frauds, which differs from being voidable.
distractorExplanations.c: Buyer's remorse is not a legal ground; a valid contract cannot be avoided because a better deal appears.

az-real-estate-readiness-check-agency-la.explanation: Fraud or lack of capacity can make a contract voidable by the protected party. Whether the contract is voidable depends on the circumstances.

options.a: Practicing law if they draft novel legal clauses beyond authorized forms
options.b: Practicing law whenever they complete any blank on a standard purchase form
options.c: Acting as the escrow agent and must hold the earnest money until closing
options.d: Required to have the buyer's attorney approve each blank before signing

distractorExplanations.b: Filling blanks on approved forms is generally permitted; it becomes law practice when drafting new legal clauses.
distractorExplanations.c: Completing a form does not make the licensee an escrow agent; who holds earnest money is set by the contract.
distractorExplanations.d: Attorney review may be recommended, but there is no general rule requiring attorney approval of each blank.

options.a: Proceed as a dual agent after giving the buyer written notice of the relationship
options.b: Switch to representing the buyer while keeping the seller's listing active for both
options.c: Not create the dual agency relationship; consider designated agency, referral, or withdrawal
options.d: Terminate the listing agreement unilaterally and refund the seller's marketing costs

distractorExplanations.a: Dual agency requires informed consent from both parties; notice to the buyer alone cannot replace the seller's consent.
distractorExplanations.b: Representing the buyer while still holding the listing is undisclosed dual agency, the exact thing the seller refused.
distractorExplanations.d: Refusing dual agency does not let the broker abandon the listing; the broker simply declines to represent the buyer.

options.a: Mixing client trust money with personal or operating funds improperly
options.b: Using client trust money for the broker's own business or personal expenses
options.c: Depositing several clients' earnest money deposits into one trust account
options.d: Holding earnest money beyond the deadline for depositing it into escrow

distractorExplanations.b: Spending trust money on the broker's own expenses is conversion, a separate and more serious violation.
distractorExplanations.c: Pooling multiple clients' funds in one properly kept trust account is permitted; mixing in broker money is not.
distractorExplanations.d: Late deposit is a timeliness violation of trust-account rules, not the mixing of trust and personal funds.

options.a: May hold unequal shares and typically lack survivorship unless specified
options.b: Must acquire title at the same time and through the same deed
options.c: Hold a right of survivorship so a deceased owner's share passes to the others
options.d: Need consent of all co-owners before selling their own share

distractorExplanations.b: Unity of time and title are joint tenancy requirements; tenants in common may acquire at different times.
distractorExplanations.c: Survivorship is the hallmark of joint tenancy; a tenant in common's share passes to heirs or devisees.
distractorExplanations.d: A tenant in common may sell an undivided share without the other co-owners' consent.

options.a: Land bordering a lake, sea, or ocean with still or tidal water
options.b: Rights to minerals, oil, and gas beneath the land's surface
options.c: Land bordering flowing water such as a river or stream
options.d: Rights to use the airspace above the land for development

distractorExplanations.a: Rights along lakes, seas, and oceans are littoral rights; riparian rights concern flowing rivers and streams.
distractorExplanations.b: Subsurface mineral rights are a separate bundle of rights and are unrelated to water boundaries.
distractorExplanations.d: Air rights cover space above the land and can be severed, but they are not water rights.

options.a: 1% of the purchase price
options.b: 1% of the loan amount
options.c: 1% of the down payment
options.d: 1% of the interest rate

distractorExplanations.a: Points are based on the loan amount, not the price; with a down payment the loan is smaller than the price.
distractorExplanations.c: The down payment is the buyer's equity, not the base for points; points are 1% of the amount borrowed.
distractorExplanations.d: A point is a fee on the loan amount; it may buy down the rate but is not computed from the rate.

options.a: Both interest and principal so the balance declines over the term
options.b: Interest each month, with the full principal due as a balloon at maturity
options.c: Principal only, with interest added to the balance each month
options.d: Interest and principal in payments that increase each year of the term

distractorExplanations.b: That describes an interest-only or straight term loan with a balloon, not a fully amortizing loan.
distractorExplanations.c: Adding unpaid interest to the balance is negative amortization, the opposite of an amortizing payment.
distractorExplanations.d: Rising payments describe a graduated payment mortgage; a fixed-rate amortizing payment stays level.

options.a: Conventional LTV is high (commonly above 80%)
options.b: An FHA loan is used with a down payment of 3.5%
options.c: A VA loan is used with no down payment at all
options.d: Conventional LTV falls to 78% of original value

distractorExplanations.b: FHA loans carry the government's mortgage insurance premium (MIP), not private mortgage insurance.
distractorExplanations.c: VA loans are guaranteed by the VA and do not require PMI even with no down payment; a funding fee applies instead.
distractorExplanations.d: 78% of original value is when borrower-paid PMI terminates under the Homeowners Protection Act, not when it starts.

options.a: Disclosure of the APR and finance charges to consumer borrowers
options.b: Maximum interest rates that may be charged on certain loans
options.c: Lending discrimination based on race, sex, or marital status
options.d: Fees for referring settlement services in residential loans

distractorExplanations.a: Credit cost disclosure is the Truth in Lending Act; usury laws cap the rate itself.
distractorExplanations.c: Credit discrimination is governed by the Equal Credit Opportunity Act, not usury laws.
distractorExplanations.d: Referral fees and kickbacks for settlement services are restricted by RESPA, not usury laws.

options.a: Finance a short-term gap, often between purchase of a new home and sale of an existing one
options.b: Finance construction draws as a new home is built, then convert to a permanent loan
options.c: Combine a first and second mortgage to avoid PMI on an 80/10/10 purchase
options.d: Let a buyer take over the seller's existing loan on its original terms

distractorExplanations.b: That describes a construction (construction-to-permanent) loan, which funds building rather than a sale gap.
distractorExplanations.c: That describes a piggyback loan structure used to avoid PMI, not short-term gap financing between homes.
distractorExplanations.d: That describes a loan assumption, where the buyer takes over the seller's mortgage, not a bridge loan.

options.a: The listing broker earns a commission unless the seller personally finds the buyer, in which case no fee is owed
options.b: The listing broker is owed a commission if the property sells during the term, regardless of who finds the buyer
options.c: The seller may list with several brokers at once and pays the one broker who first procures a ready buyer
options.d: The buyer's agent, rather than the listing broker, is owed the commission whenever that agent introduced the buyer

distractorExplanations.a: That describes an exclusive agency listing, where a sale the owner procures personally owes no commission.
distractorExplanations.c: That describes an open listing, where only the procuring broker is paid and several brokers may list at once.
distractorExplanations.d: Swaps the party: the exclusive right-to-sell agreement protects the listing broker's commission, not the buyer's agent's.

options.a: The seller may sell the property personally without owing any commission
options.b: The broker's compensation is the amount above a seller's net price
options.c: The broker is paid a flat fee whether or not the property sells
options.d: The broker keeps the buyer's earnest money as the commission at closing

distractorExplanations.a: That describes an exclusive agency listing; it is not why net listings are restricted.
distractorExplanations.c: That describes a flat-fee arrangement; a net listing pays the broker whatever exceeds the seller's net figure.
distractorExplanations.d: Earnest money is trust money credited per the contract; a net listing is defined by pay above the seller's net price.

az-real-estate-readiness-check-agency-la.explanation: Net listings can incentivize underpricing relative to the seller's interests and are banned or tightly regulated in many places. That structure creates conflict-of-interest concerns because the broker gains by underpricing the seller's net figure.

options.a: An obligation to purchase on stated terms within a period, usually with earnest money
options.b: A right to purchase on stated terms within a period, usually for consideration
options.c: A right of first refusal to match any offer the owner accepts
options.d: A leasehold that converts into ownership once the scheduled rent payments are made

distractorExplanations.a: That describes a bilateral purchase contract; an option gives the optionee a right, not an obligation, to buy.
distractorExplanations.c: Confuses an option with a right of first refusal, which only lets the holder match a third-party offer the owner accepts.
distractorExplanations.d: Describes a rent-to-own or contract-for-deed arrangement; an option is a purchased right to buy on fixed terms.

options.a: Exaggerated opinion that a reasonable person would not treat as a factual warranty
options.b: A misstatement of a measurable fact, such as square footage, made to induce a sale
options.c: A negligent misrepresentation the licensee should have known was untrue
options.d: An implied warranty of habitability the seller gives through the ad wording

distractorExplanations.b: A false statement of measurable fact is misrepresentation, not puffing; puffing is non-factual opinion.
distractorExplanations.c: Negligent misrepresentation involves a false fact the licensee should have verified; puffing is opinion, not fact.
distractorExplanations.d: Confuses puffing with a warranty; puffing is exaggerated opinion that a reasonable buyer would not rely on as a warranty.

options.a: Reversion
options.b: Remainder
options.c: Dower rights
options.d: Survivorship

distractorExplanations.a: Reversion is the grantor's future interest after a lesser estate such as a life estate ends, not a joint tenancy feature.
distractorExplanations.b: A remainder is a future interest that follows a life estate; joint tenancy is defined by survivorship among co-owners.
distractorExplanations.c: Dower is a surviving wife's marital interest (abolished in most states), not a feature of joint tenancy.

options.a: Owner consent and fair market value paid
options.b: Public use/purpose and just compensation
options.c: Public use, without compensation under police power
options.d: Just compensation and approval by county voters

distractorExplanations.a: Eminent domain is a forced taking; owner consent is not required, only public use and just compensation.
distractorExplanations.c: Confuses eminent domain with police-power regulation; a taking requires just compensation.
distractorExplanations.d: No voter approval is required; the constitutional tests are public use and just compensation.

az-real-estate-readiness-check-property-.explanation: Takings require public purpose and just compensation under the Constitution. This comes from the Fifth Amendment takings framework.

options.a: Upon the death of the measuring life
options.b: Upon the death of the remainderman
options.c: When the life tenant sells the property
options.d: After a fixed term of 99 years

distractorExplanations.b: Wrong party: the remainderman holds the future interest; the life estate is measured by the life tenant's life.
distractorExplanations.c: A life tenant can convey the interest, but the buyer's estate still ends at the measuring life's death.
distractorExplanations.d: A fixed term describes a leasehold estate for years, not a life estate.

az-real-estate-readiness-check-property-.explanation: Life estates are measured by a life; remainder/reversion follows. The estate may be defined otherwise in the grant (e.g., pur autre vie).

options.a: The insurer's promise to defend title against covered claims
options.b: A deed that conveys title without any warranties from the grantor
options.c: A claim, encumbrance, or defect that may impair marketability
options.d: A court action used to settle competing ownership claims

distractorExplanations.a: That describes title insurance coverage, not a defect that clouds title.
distractorExplanations.b: That is a quitclaim deed, which is often used to remove a cloud rather than being one.
distractorExplanations.d: That is a quiet-title action, the remedy for a cloud, not the cloud itself.

options.a: Permission to deviate from a zoning requirement due to hardship
options.b: Permanent change of the zoning map for an entire district
options.c: Prior use allowed to continue after a new zoning law is adopted
options.d: Use the zoning code allows in a district subject to stated conditions

distractorExplanations.c: That is a legal nonconforming (grandfathered) use, not a variance granted for hardship.
distractorExplanations.d: That is a conditional use or special-use permit, which the code anticipates; a variance relieves a hardship.
distractorExplanations.b: That is rezoning/amendment.

az-real-estate-readiness-check-property-.explanation: Variances grant relief from strict zoning application in hardship cases. The variance is granted by the zoning authority (e.g., a board of adjustment).

options.a: Prohibiting discrimination in mortgage lending based on race or sex
options.b: Requiring APR disclosure and a right to rescind certain refinances
options.c: Setting the maximum interest rate lenders may charge on home loans
options.d: Banning certain kickbacks and requiring settlement cost disclosures

distractorExplanations.a: That is the Equal Credit Opportunity Act and Fair Housing Act, not RESPA's settlement-cost focus.
distractorExplanations.b: APR disclosure and rescission rights come from the Truth in Lending Act, not RESPA.
distractorExplanations.c: Interest-rate ceilings come from state usury laws; RESPA does not cap rates.

az-real-estate-readiness-check-finance-a.explanation: RESPA addresses settlement services, kickbacks, and related disclosures (with TRID integration for many loans). These protections apply in covered federally related transactions.

options.a: Adjusts on the margin alone, with the index fixed at closing
options.b: Can adjust based on an index plus margin, subject to caps
options.c: Can adjust when the borrower's credit score changes, subject to caps
options.d: Is fixed for the term while the payment changes with escrow

distractorExplanations.a: Reverses the formula: the margin is fixed at closing and the index moves.
distractorExplanations.c: ARM adjustments follow a published index, not the borrower's later credit score.
distractorExplanations.d: That describes a fixed-rate loan with escrow changes; an ARM's interest rate itself adjusts.

options.a: Borrower default on the mortgage note
options.b: Fire, wind, and flood damage to the structure
options.c: Covered title defects and claims against ownership
options.d: Undisclosed defects in the home's systems found after closing

distractorExplanations.a: Default risk is covered by mortgage insurance (PMI/FHA MIP), not title insurance.
distractorExplanations.b: Casualty damage is covered by hazard and flood insurance, not title insurance.
distractorExplanations.d: Physical system failures are the subject of a home warranty or disclosure claim, not title insurance.

az-real-estate-readiness-check-finance-a.explanation: Owner's/lender's title policies insure against covered title risks, not casualty. Coverage is defined by the owner's or lender's policy terms and exceptions.

options.a: The seller is charged; it reduces the seller's net proceeds
options.b: The item is prorated and split evenly between buyer and seller
options.c: The buyer receives a credit reducing cash to close
options.d: The buyer is charged; it increases cash needed

distractorExplanations.a: Swaps the party: a buyer debit charges the buyer, not the seller.
distractorExplanations.b: Proration splits an expense by time, and each share then appears as a debit or credit; it is not what 'debit' means.
distractorExplanations.c: That describes a credit.

az-real-estate-readiness-check-finance-a.explanation: Debits charge a party; buyer debits typically increase funds due at closing. A debit to the seller, by contrast, reduces the seller's proceeds.

options.a: Buy and sell existing mortgages, improving liquidity for originators
options.b: Originate new purchase loans directly to borrowers at the closing table
options.c: Insure lenders against borrower default on low-down-payment loans
options.d: Set the federal funds rate that lenders use to price mortgages

distractorExplanations.b: Originating loans to borrowers is the primary mortgage market, not the secondary market.
distractorExplanations.c: Default insurance is the role of PMI or FHA mortgage insurance, not the secondary market.
distractorExplanations.d: The Federal Reserve sets the federal funds target; the secondary market buys and sells loans.

options.a: May be required or strongly expected, but does not excuse license law violations
options.b: Covers fines the commission imposes for license law violations
options.c: Covers intentional misrepresentation claims as long as the policy premium is current
options.d: Satisfies the state's recovery fund contribution for each licensee

distractorExplanations.b: E&O policies cover negligence claims by clients, not regulatory fines for violations.
distractorExplanations.c: E&O excludes intentional fraud; it covers negligent errors and omissions.
distractorExplanations.d: Confuses E&O with the recovery fund; the fund is a separate statutory program for consumer claims.

az-real-estate-readiness-check-az-licens.explanation: E&O manages negligence risk; it is not a license to violate the law. Whether it is required depends on firm and state risk practices.

options.a: Performs administrative tasks and may negotiate repairs if the agent approves the terms
options.b: May show listed homes and answer pricing questions if a licensee is on the phone
options.c: Performs administrative tasks under supervision and must not negotiate unless licensed
options.d: Must hold a broker license because the role handles trust account documents

distractorExplanations.a: Negotiating repair terms is a licensed activity; agent approval does not let an unlicensed coordinator do it.
distractorExplanations.b: Showing property and discussing price are licensed activities; remote supervision does not change that.
distractorExplanations.d: Administrative paperwork does not require a broker license; only licensed activities such as negotiating do.

options.a: Compliant if the agent's license number is shown
options.b: Noncompliant with brokerage identification rules
options.c: Allowed on personal social media accounts
options.d: Compliant once the broker approves the ad verbally

distractorExplanations.a: A license number does not satisfy the rule that ads identify the responsible brokerage.
distractorExplanations.c: Brokerage identification rules apply to licensee ads on social media too.
distractorExplanations.d: Broker approval does not cure omitting the brokerage name; the ad itself must identify the firm.

options.a: Follow the instruction but note the defect in the file to protect the brokerage
options.b: Have the seller sign a hold-harmless letter, then omit the defect as instructed
options.c: Refuse to conceal legally required disclosures and consider withdrawal
options.d: Tell buyers about the defect orally but leave it off the written disclosure

distractorExplanations.a: Documenting a defect internally while concealing it from buyers is still participating in misrepresentation.
distractorExplanations.b: An indemnity letter cannot authorize the licensee to conceal a known material defect.
distractorExplanations.d: Required disclosures must be complete on the disclosure form; oral hints do not satisfy the duty.

az-real-estate-readiness-check-az-licens.explanation: Licensees cannot participate in fraud; illegal instructions must be refused. Withdrawal is appropriate if the seller persists.

options.a: Satisfies the broker's supervision duty so no further review of individual agents is needed
options.b: Shields the broker from liability for an agent's license law violations
options.c: Must be filed with the Department for approval before agents are hired
options.d: Documents supervision standards and compliant procedures for affiliated licensees

distractorExplanations.a: A manual supports supervision but does not replace the broker's ongoing duty to review agents' work.
distractorExplanations.b: A written policy does not immunize the broker; inadequate supervision can still lead to discipline.
distractorExplanations.c: The manual is an internal supervision tool kept by the broker, not a document pre-approved by the regulator.

options.a: Be registered/comply with branch office rules when required
options.b: Operate under the main office's license with no separate notice
options.c: Use a separate trade name so clients know it is a distinct office
options.d: Be managed by any salesperson with one year of experience

distractorExplanations.b: Branch offices generally need registration or a branch license, not silent operation under the main office.
distractorExplanations.c: A branch must operate under the brokerage's licensed name; a separate trade name would mislead clients.
distractorExplanations.d: Branch supervision requires a qualified broker-level manager, not any experienced salesperson.

az-real-estate-readiness-check-az-licens.explanation: Branch locations often need registration and supervision. Arizona branch rules are administered by the Arizona Department of Real Estate.

options.a: Acceptable puffing because it states the firm's opinion of its results
options.b: Allowed if the broker's name appears in the advertisement
options.c: Compliant if one past sale closed 20% above list
options.d: Likely deceptive unless substantiated and carefully qualified

distractorExplanations.a: A specific, measurable performance claim is a factual assertion, not opinion-based puffing.
distractorExplanations.b: Brokerage identification is a separate rule; naming the broker does not make a false claim truthful.
distractorExplanations.c: A single cherry-picked sale does not substantiate an 'every time' claim.

options.a: Which licensing fees a broker must pay to open a limited-service brokerage office
options.b: How commissions must be split between the listing broker and each cooperating broker
options.c: When a salesperson may perform services without a supervising broker
options.d: What services a listing broker must still provide even in limited-service listings

distractorExplanations.a: Minimum-service laws set required duties to clients, not licensing fees for opening an office.
distractorExplanations.b: Commission splits are negotiated between brokers; minimum-service laws address services owed to the client.
distractorExplanations.c: Minimum-service laws do not remove broker supervision; they define services a listing broker must still provide.

options.a: Disclose it because confidentiality duties end when the transaction closes
options.b: Give it out once the buyer explains the dispute in writing
options.c: Protect confidential client information and not disclose without authority
options.d: Provide it if the buyer's agent requests it on the buyer's behalf

distractorExplanations.a: Confidentiality of a client's personal information can survive closing; the deal closing does not end it.
distractorExplanations.b: A written explanation from the buyer is not client authority or a legal requirement to disclose.
distractorExplanations.d: A request through the buyer's agent does not create authority to disclose the seller's private information.

az-real-estate-readiness-check-az-licens.explanation: Confidentiality can survive closing for non-public personal information. Disclosure is appropriate only with client authority or a legal requirement (e.g., subpoena).

options.a: Discipline by the Arizona Corporation Commission's securities division
options.b: Review by the Arizona Board of Appraisal
options.c: Removal from the MLS by the local association only
options.d: Disciplinary action by Arizona Department of Real Estate

distractorExplanations.a: Wrong agency: the Corporation Commission regulates corporations and utilities, not real estate licensees.
distractorExplanations.b: Wrong agency: the Board of Appraisal licenses appraisers, not real estate salespersons and brokers.
distractorExplanations.c: MLS sanctions are private; deceptive ads also expose the licensee to state license discipline.

options.a: A matter for the Department to decide, which can order one broker to pay
options.b: Settled by the escrow agent releasing the buyer's deposit to whichever broker is owed
options.c: A civil/contract matter between the brokers (or via MLS/association processes)
options.d: A matter for the buyer and seller to resolve before closing can occur

distractorExplanations.a: The regulator disciplines licensees but does not adjudicate commission disputes between brokers.
distractorExplanations.b: Earnest money belongs to the transaction under the contract; it cannot be redirected to settle a broker fee dispute.
distractorExplanations.d: Wrong parties: the commission dispute is between the brokers, not the principals.

az-real-estate-readiness-check-az-licens.explanation: Commission disputes are between licensees/firms; earnest money still follows contract/escrow rules. It is not a reason to withhold a buyer's earnest money unlawfully.

options.a: follow transfer procedures so the license is properly affiliated
options.b: Let the license expire and then reapply under the new broker
options.c: Notify only the old broker, since the Department is not involved
options.d: Take their active listings to the new broker without client consent

distractorExplanations.b: No new application is needed; a transfer of affiliation keeps the existing license active.
distractorExplanations.c: The regulator must record the affiliation change; notifying the old broker alone is not enough.
distractorExplanations.d: Listings belong to the brokerage, so they cannot move with the agent without the firm's and client's consent.

az-real-estate-readiness-check-az-licens.explanation: Affiliation changes require regulatory notice/transfer steps. Transfer steps include notifying the Arizona Department of Real Estate.

options.a: Disclose licensee status only if the price is below the listing price
options.b: Have a different agent in the firm handle the offer, with no further disclosure to the seller
options.c: Waive their share of the commission, which removes any disclosure duty
options.d: Disclose their licensee status and follow any required consent/disclosure rules

distractorExplanations.a: Licensee status must be disclosed in any purchase, not only below list price.
distractorExplanations.b: Using a colleague does not remove the duty to disclose the buyer's licensee status and interest.
distractorExplanations.c: Waiving compensation does not cure the conflict; disclosure of licensee status is still required.
